title: Merchandise Purchases — Sales Audit Note on Spreading Order-Level Amounts over Units
content:
**Rule.** In Merchandise Purchases, amounts that belong to a whole order are spread over the purchase records sharing its order number:

1. A coupon or order-level promotion is allocated in proportion to each unit's price before the discount, each share rounded half up to the cent, with any rounding remainder placed on the highest-priced unit. The allocated share is already reflected in each unit's selling price.
2. Finch Notes applied to the order are allocated the same way, and each unit records the Finch Note value allocated to it.
3. A mixed-tender transaction is recorded with the tender shown as mixed on its purchase records, and with one payment entry per tender per unit, allocated the same way.
4. A refund of one unit returns only that unit's allocated amounts. When a coupon required a minimum purchase that the units kept no longer meet, the coupon is not taken back.

## Worked allocation (hypothetical figures)

A $10.00 coupon on an order of three units priced $50.00, $25.00 and $15.00 before the discount (together $90.00):

| Unit | Price before discount | Exact proportional share | Rounded half up to the cent | After placing the remainder |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A (highest-priced) | $50.00 | $5.5556 | $5.56 | $5.55 |
| B | $25.00 | $2.7778 | $2.78 | $2.78 |
| C | $15.00 | $1.6667 | $1.67 | $1.67 |

The rounded shares total $10.01, one cent more than the coupon; that remainder is taken up on unit A, the highest-priced unit, so the shares total exactly $10.00. Unit A's selling price is then $50.00 less $5.55, that is $44.45.

## Points of judgement

- **Returning unit B alone.** Only unit B's own amounts come back; units A and C keep their shares.
- **A coupon with a minimum spend.** If the coupon had required a $75.00 minimum and the customer returns unit A, the coupon is not taken back from units B and C.
- **Mixed tender.** A unit paid partly by gift card and partly by debit card carries one payment entry for each of the two tenders.
